Key unresolved questions concern the relative contributions of plasma membrane and ER channels, the effects of sustained inhibition, and consequences for other islet hormones. We discuss how addressing these questions can establish whether TALK channel modulation improves glucose-responsive insulin secretion and preserves islet function, and whether these effects translate into sustained improvements in glucose homeostasis in vivo.

articles.title: Appraisal of clinical practice guidelines and consensus statements on aspirin in pregnancy: a systematic review using the AGREE II instrument.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Recommendations regarding the use of aspirin in obstetrics vary across clinical practice guidelines and consensus statements of differing quality. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the quality of these documents, with particular focus on the recommended daily dosage, timing of initiation, and cessation of aspirin in the obstetric setting. This study employed a systematic review and quality appraisal approach using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation (AGREE) II methodology. METHODS: The study included the most recent versions of all international and national/regional clinical practice guidelines and consensus statements on aspirin use in pregnancy, published in English or Chinese. Data were retrieved from PubMed (11 April 2025), three Chinese academic databases (the Chinese Medical Association Database, Wanfang Data and China National Knowledge Infrastructure) and four guideline databases (11 April 2025). Two reviewers independently screened the searched items and extracted data. Four reviewers independently scored documents using AGREE II. Recommendations from all documents were tabulated and visualized using a color-coded grid. RESULTS: A total of 32 documents were include, encompassing six obstetric conditions: Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS), Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR), advanced maternal age, pregnancy loss, stillbirth and hypertension/pre-eclampsia. The included documents demonstrated strong performance in the domains of scope and purpose (median score: 89.67%, inter-quartile range [IQR] 61.11%-98.61%) and clarity of presentation (median 87.93%, IQR 50%-100%). The editorial independence domain also received relatively high score (median 73.59%, IQR 0%-100%). However, performance was lower in the domain of applicability (median 45.08%, IQR 0%-89.58%). Although aspirin 75-100 mg daily represents the most commonly recommended dosage, a broad range of dosing recommendations exists across most clinical scenarios. However, considerable controversy existed regarding the optimal timing of discontinuation, particularly in cases of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy/pre-eclampsia. CONCLUSION: Guidelines and consensus statements, which were generally of relatively high quality, demonstrated that most documents support the use of aspirin for specific obstetric complications. Given these substantial variations in dosage ranges, treatment timing, and combination therapy recommendations, developing standardized, evidence-based protocols is essential to improve the consistency and quality of aspirin therapy in obstetric care. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://inplasy.com/inplasy-2025-4-0017, identifier INPLASY202540017.

articles.title: From hope to adoption: an industry perspective on the maturation of new approach methodologies.
Response to a letter to the editor entitled 'Long-acting relaxin for pulmonary hypertension: From systemic pharmacodynamics to disease-site pharmacology'.
The Role of Oxidative Stress and Antioxidant Signaling in Skin Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Oxidative stress represents a prevalent form of cellular and tissue damage, arising from an imbalance between diminished antioxidant defense mechanisms and elevated reactive species production. This pathological condition occurs following exposure to endogenous or exogenous stressors, triggering the intracellular accumulation of excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), reactive nitrogen species (RNS), and other free radicals that ultimately induce cellular and tissue injury. Skin wounds are a disruption or interruption of normal skin anatomical organization and functional continuity. They can be categorized into acute and chronic skin wounds based on the time of healing, and consists of four overlapping stages: hemostasis, inflammation, proliferation, and remodeling phases. Any mistake in any stage can lead to delayed skin wound healing, non-healing ulcers or even scar formation, which happens especially easily in diabetic patients. Impaired skin wound repair represents a significant clinical concern that may precipitate severe sequelae such as localized soft tissue infection (cellulitis), tissue necrosis (gangrene), and systemic inflammatory response (sepsis). These complications frequently culminate in the necessity for surgical limb amputation, particularly in the lower extremities. These negative consequences impose psychological and economic burdens on patients and countries. Oxidative stress plays a regulatory role throughout all four phases of cutaneous wound repair through multiple signaling cascades, including but not limited to the Keap1/Nrf2/ARE pathway and the PI3K/AKT pathway. In this review, we describe the relationships between oxidative stress and skin wound healing process, in order to provide the potential mechanisms for new options of treatment in skin wound healing via oxidative stress.

articles.title: Preclinical Evidence for Ligusticum chuanxiong-Derived Interventions in Experimental Spinal Cord Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Animal Studies.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Ligusticum chuanxiong is a traditional medicinal herb widely used for conditions related to blood circulation, inflammation, and neurological dysfunction. Its extracts and major bioactive compounds, including tetramethylpyrazine and ferulic acid, have shown neuroprotective potential in experimental spinal cord injury (SCI). However, the broader preclinical evidence remains incompletely characterized. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to systematically evaluate the efficacy and potential mechanisms of Ligusticum chuanxiong-derived interventions in experimental SCI METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP were systematically searched for animal studies evaluating Ligusticum chuanxiong-derived interventions in SCI models. The primary outcomes were BBB locomotor scores and inclined plane test performance. Secondary outcomes included inflammatory, oxidative stress, apoptotic, glial, and neuronal markers. Risk of bias was assessed using the SYRCLE tool, and certainty of evidence using an adapted GRADE approach. RESULTS: Forty animal studies were included. Ligusticum chuanxiong-derived interventions were associated with improved BBB scores at 3, 7, 14, 21, and 28 days after SCI, as well as improved inclined plane test performance from 7 to 21 days after injury. Mechanistic outcomes showed reduced IL-1β, MDA, and TUNEL-positive cells, together with increased SOD levels, suggesting potential neuroprotective effects through anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and cell death-reducing mechanisms. At 28 days, immunofluorescence-based analyses indicated higher NeuN expression, whereas the pooled GFAP difference did not reach statistical significance; substantial heterogeneity limited certainty; caspase-3 expression was lower at 3 and 7 days, each based on three studies. Sensitivity analyses indicated that the BBB findings were generally robust, although potential publication bias or small-study effects were detected at several time points. An exploratory dose-time analysis of tetramethylpyrazine suggested that BBB effect sizes may increase over time, but the available evidence was insufficient to define an optimal dose. CONCLUSION: Ligusticum chuanxiong-derived interventions may improve motor recovery after experimental SCI, potentially through modulation of inflammation, oxidative stress, and cell death. Further rigorously designed animal studies are needed to clarify active constituents, therapeutic windows, optimal dosing strategies, and translational potential.

articles.title: The genus Dendropanax (Araliaceae): A comprehensive review of the botany, traditional uses, phytochemistry, pharmacology, quality control, and economic importance.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The genus Dendropanax is primary distributed in East Asia and tropical America, with some species being characteristic medicinal plants and economic crops in China and South Korea, exhibiting anti-inflammatory effects, alleviating rheumatic pain and migraine. However, reviews on the phytochemistry and pharmacology of this genus are scarce and unsystematic, hindering the rational application and in-depth development of these plants. AIMS OF THE REVIEW: This review comprehensively reviews the botany, traditional uses, phytochemistry, pharmacology, quality control, and economic importance of the genus, to provide a robust scientific foundation for its clinical application, quality control, and rational development. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic literature review of the genus Dendropanax was conducted using Chinese resources (e.g., books, CNKI, Wanfang, Weipu) and international databases (e.g., Web of Science, SciFinder, PubMed, ScienceDirect, Springer), followed by a systematic summary of the retrieved literature. RESULTS: The genus Dendropanax comprises ninety-seven accepted species, among which D. dentiger and D. proteus are traditional medicinal plants native to China, while D. morbiferus is a medicinal plant native to Korea. Since 1973, a total of one hundred and forty-seven chemical constituents have been isolated and identified from the genus Dendropanax, including forty-nine phenylpropanoids, twenty-one phenol derivatives, seventeen fatty acids and fatty alcohols, seventeen polyacetylenes, eleven flavonoids, nine triterpenoids, four sesquiterpenoids, six alkaloids, and thirteen others, across six species: D. dentiger (seventy-eight), D. proteus (sixteen), D. morbiferus (sixty-six), D. arboreus (seven), D. trifidus (four), and D. querceti (one). Additionally, seventy-eight, thirty-three, twenty-nine, and four volatile oil components were identified from D. arboreus, D. morbifera, D. gonatopodus, and D. capillaris, respectively. The genus Dendropanax exhibits a wide range of pharmacological activities, including anti-inflammatory, anti-oxidative, anti-tumor, hepatoprotective, anti-obesity, anti-diabetic, memory-improving, anti-hyperuricemic, neuroprotective, and renoprotective effects, but only involving six species: D. dentiger, D. proteus, D. morbiferus, D. arboreus, D. capillaris, and D. trifidus. Currently, only fingerprint analysis and HPLC content determination have been studied for D. dentiger and D. morbiferus, but no relevant quality standard protocols have been established. CONCLUSION: The Dendropanax genus exhibits diverse pharmacological activities and a diverse array of chemical constituents, but comprehensive research remains scarce and superficial, especially regarding the pharmacodynamic substances and mechanisms associated with traditional functions. Urgent investigations are required into the phytochemistry, pharmacology, and mechanism of Dendropanax species, as well as the development of robust, forward-looking, and practical quality standard protocols, to provide a scientific basis for their clinical application and rational development.

articles.title: Aldo-keto reductase family 1 member B10 in solid tumors: lipid metabolic reprogramming, immune remodeling, and targeted therapy.
articles.abstract: Aldo-keto reductase family 1 member B10 (AKR1B10), an NADPH-dependent aldo-keto reductase, has emerged as a context-dependent metabolic stress regulator with important implications for therapeutic resistance and tumor immune remodeling in solid tumors. By neutralizing lipid-derived aldehydes such as 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE), AKR1B10 limits lipid-derived carbonyl stress and may reduce ferroptosis susceptibility in defined tumor contexts. It also stabilizes acetyl-CoA carboxylase α, thereby sustaining de novo lipogenesis (DNL). In addition, AKR1B10 has been linked to increased glycolysis-associated lactate production in specific tumor settings. This increase in lactate can promote histone lactylation-mediated epigenetic reprogramming. Together with reported associations between AKR1B10 and immune-cell infiltration or function, these metabolic effects may contribute to tumor immune remodeling in a context-dependent manner. Aberrant AKR1B10 expression has been associated with tumor progression and therapeutic resistance in several solid tumors, including hepatocellular carcinoma, non-small-cell lung cancer, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, and cholangiocarcinoma. This review systematically examines the structural biology, transcriptional regulation, and tumor-intrinsic and microenvironmental functions of AKR1B10. It further evaluates its tumor-type-specific diagnostic and prognostic potential and discusses emerging inhibitor strategies. Nonetheless, key challenges remain, including the tissue-specific functional duality of AKR1B10, the demand for inhibitors selective over the structurally homologous AKR1B1, and limited causal evidence linking AKR1B10 to immune remodeling in tumors. Future research should integrate multimodal spatial omics, immunocompetent tumor models, and rational combination therapy designs to advance AKR1B10 from a metabolic enzyme into a clinically actionable target for precision oncology.

articles.title: CD14 in glioblastoma and temozolomide resistance: what the evidence does and does not support.
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM), designated as central nervous system World Health Organization grade 4, is the most lethal adult brain tumor, with a median overall survival (OS) of 14.6 months despite resection, radiotherapy, and temozolomide (TMZ). The benefit of TMZ is largely confined to the 45 % of GBMs carrying a methylated O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter, where, in 206 assessable patients from the pivotal Phase III trial (reported in 2005), adding TMZ to radiotherapy extended median OS from 15.3 to 21.7 months, whereas MGMT-unmethylated tumors derived no significant benefit; these are historical estimates from a single trial subset. Resistance arises through MGMT-mediated repair of O6-methylguanine, MSH6 loss or mutation affecting mismatch repair, glioma stem cell repopulation, and an immunosuppressive microenvironment enriched with CD14+ myeloid cells, including tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), monocytes, and monocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells. CD14 is a glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored co-receptor for Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), expressed constitutively on monocytes, macrophages, and microglia and also by a subset of glioma cells. Because CD14 has no intracellular domain, it cannot signal independently of a partner receptor; CD14-dependent signaling through TLR4/MD-2 has been proposed to contribute to nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) activation, pro-survival transcription, MGMT-related resistance pathways, and immunosuppressive myeloid polarization, although no study has shown this in glioma cells, the link to TMZ resistance remains hypothetical, and CD14 alone does not define an M2-like TAM phenotype. This review synthesizes over 50 publications across CD14 biology in the brain, CD14 expression across the immune and tumor-cell landscape of GBM, CD14-associated inflammatory signaling, TMZ resistance mechanisms, CD14-related influences on TMZ sensitivity, and candidate therapeutic strategies. Of those strategies, only IC14 (atibuclimab) targets CD14 directly; TLR4, NF-κB, signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 and colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor inhibition, TAM repolarization, poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibition, and checkpoint blockade act on the partner receptor, on shared downstream nodes or on the CD14-enriched myeloid compartment, and are therefore described as CD14-associated rather than CD14-targeted. CD14+ myeloid populations are associated with aggressive GBM biology, whereas the proposed glioma-cell-intrinsic CD14 → TLR4/MD-2 → NF-κB → MGMT cascade rests on a single 2003 expression dataset and has never been tested by CD14 loss-of-function, gain-of-function, rescue or lineage-specific in vivo experiments. The purpose of this review is to document that gap and to specify the experiments that would close it, not to advocate CD14 as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Antibiotic-derived peptides delivered by nanocarriers as multifunctional pharmacological modulators in chronic wound healing.
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds, particularly those associated with diabetes and metabolic disorders, represent a persistent therapeutic challenge characterized by sustained inflammation, microbial colonization, oxidative imbalance, and impaired angiogenesis. Current pharmacological management relies heavily on antimicrobial agents; however, conventional antibiotics primarily address infection and exert limited influence on host pathways governing tissue repair. Recent studies indicate that peptide derivatives originating from antibiotic scaffolds retain membrane-targeting properties while also interacting with immune, redox, and cellular signaling networks relevant to wound resolution. This review examines antibiotic-derived peptides as pharmacologically active molecules whose therapeutic profile can be reshaped through nanocarrier-based delivery. Liposomal and lipid-based nanocarriers are discussed not only as drug transport systems but also as modulators of pharmacokinetics, spatial distribution, and microenvironmental exposure within the wound bed. Such systems enable sustained local presentation of peptides, potentially influencing macrophage polarization, cytokine balance, angiogenic signaling, and extracellular matrix remodeling in addition to antimicrobial effects. By integrating evidence from peptide pharmacology, wound pathophysiology, and controlled-release science, we evaluate how structural optimization and carrier design jointly determine biological activity in chronic wound settings. Key challenges, including proteolytic instability, dose localization, safety considerations, and translational scalability are analyzed to define the boundaries of clinical applicability. This perspective highlights the repositioning of antibiotic-derived peptides from infection-focused agents toward multifunctional regulators of tissue repair, providing a mechanistic basis for future pharmacological development in chronic wound therapy.

articles.title: Engineering the skin barrier: reprogramming stratum corneum structure for next-generation dermal drug delivery.
articles.abstract: The stratum corneum (SC) is now increasingly recognized as a dynamic regulatory interface, rather than a passive barrier, for dermal drug delivery. Permeability is controlled by coordinated lipid organization, corneocyte maturation, hydration control, enzymatic processing and junctional signaling, all of which are altered in inflammatory, genetic and age-related skin disorders. Traditional methods for penetration enhancement mainly function by disrupting this architecture, but this non-specific disruption can compromise barrier integrity, cause increased irritation and limit its use in repeated or long-term therapy. This sets up an obvious need for techniques that control, not just break, the skin barrier. In this review, we put forward the idea of engineering the skin barrier as a mechanism-driven strategy for reversible and targeted control of SC permeability and repair. It combines current knowledge on barrier biology with advances in biomimetic materials, responsive delivery systems, extracellular vesicles, smart hydrogels, organotypic models and computational design, and assesses how barrier function can be modulated with greater spatial, temporal and disease-specific precision. Special attention is paid to the translational gaps that currently limit this field, including proof of reversibility, standardized barrier assessment, interpatient variability, and regulatory definition. Skin barrier engineering is typically framed as a safer and more flexible paradigm for next-generation personalized dermal therapeutics.

articles.title: Danggui-Shaoyao-San Alleviates Hyperlipidemia-Induced Vascular Endothelial Barrier Dysfunction and Modulates the Rap1/PI3K/AKT Pathway in ApoE-/- Mice.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Hyperlipidemia (HL) is a major cardiovascular risk factor that can induce early endothelial dysfunction and compromise vascular endothelial barrier integrity. Danggui-Shaoyao-San (DSS), a traditional Chinese herbal formula, has shown potential vascular protective effects. However, the circulating DSS-associated constituents and molecular pathways potentially involved in its protective effects against HL-induced endothelial barrier dysfunction remain incompletely understood. MATERIALS AND METHODS: ApoE-/- mice fed a high-fat diet (HFD) were used to establish a model of HL-associated vascular endothelial barrier injury and to evaluate the effects of different doses of DSS. UPLC-Q-TOF-MS was used to characterize DSS-associated constituents detected in serum. Metabolic parameters, inflammatory markers, vascular permeability, aortic histopathology, endothelial ultrastructure, and junctional protein expression were evaluated. Transcriptomic analysis and molecular docking were integrated to explore potential targets and signaling pathways. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) was subsequently performed to evaluate the direct binding of representative serum constituents to RAP1B. Rap1-GTP pull-down, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence analyses were further used to assess Rap1 activation, PI3K/AKT phosphorylation, and endothelial junctional proteins. RESULTS: Mass spectrometry enabled the putative annotation of 19 DSS-associated serum constituents. DSS treatment alleviated HFD-induced metabolic derangements and systemic inflammation, reduced aortic permeability, and preserved endothelial morphology and junctional integrity. Transcriptomic analysis and molecular docking analyses highlighted Ras-related protein 1 (Rap1) and PI3K/AKT-related signaling for subsequent experimental investigation. SPR analysis revealed concentration-dependent binding of paeoniflorin, albiflorin, and ligustilide to RAP1B, with apparent dissociation constants (K_D) of 4.158, 4.240, and 28.71 μM, respectively. Rap1 activation, quantified as the GTP-Rap1/total Rap1A/1B ratio, was reduced in the HFD model group and increased following DSS treatment. The DSS-associated increase in Rap1 activation were accompanied by increased PI3K and AKT phosphorylation and expression of endothelial junctional proteins, including ZO-1, occludin, claudin-1, and VE-cadherin. CONCLUSION: DSS alleviated HL-associated vascular endothelial barrier dysfunction in HFD-fed ApoE-/- mice, accompanied by improvements in metabolic homeostasis and preservation of endothelial junctional integrity. The in vitro binding of selected serum constituents to recombinant RAP1B, together with restored Rap1 activation and increased PI3K/AKT phosphorylation, is consistent with the potential involvement of Rap1-associated signaling in the vascular protective effects of DSS. These findings provide preclinical evidence supporting further investigation of DSS for hyperlipidemia-associated vascular injury.

articles.title: Solubility profiling of therapeutic peptides by Taylor dispersion induced precipitation using nanoliter sample volumes.
articles.abstract: Therapeutic peptides are emerging as an important class of pharmaceutical compounds able to bridge the gap between small molecules and large biologics. Although modern peptide synthesis protocols have significantly increased the throughput of drug discovery; physicochemical assessment of the peptides' robustness with respect to developability into final drugs remains both material- and labor-intensive. Here we present an automated micro-capillary solubility assay based on Taylor dispersion able to quantify solubility using µg amounts of peptide from a single stock. We demonstrate the assay's utility with two families of therapeutic peptides targeting obesity. Together with solubility assessment, the methodology generates data on self-association and identifies glass-surface binding compounds. Combined, this information allows us to identify types of oligomerization behavior both within and across the peptide families, rationalizing differences in solubility and biophysical properties. This platform therefore represents a valuable tool in early screening and characterization.

articles.title: Mapping the Molecular Interaction Profile of 5-(1,3,4-Oxadiazol-2-yl)-Substituted Pyrimidine Hybrids in Diabetes Mellitus: Synthetic Development, Enzyme Kinetics, Molecular Recognition, In Vivo Toxicology and Therapeutic Translation.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a major metabolic disorder characterized by persistent hyperglycemia and remains a significant therapeutic challenge. Inhibition of α-amylase and α-glucosidase, key enzymes involved in carbohydrate digestion, represents an effective strategy for controlling postprandial glucose levels. In the present study, a novel series of pyrimidine-oxadiazole hybrid derivatives was designed, synthesized, structurally characterized, and evaluated using complementary experimental and computational approaches. The synthesized compounds exhibited promising inhibitory activity against both enzymes, with compound 5 having IC50 = 5.20 ± 0.10 μM and 5.90 ± 0.30 μM for α-amylase and α-glucosidase, respectively,emerging as the most potent derivative against α-amylase and α-glucosidase, showing greater activity than the reference drug acarbose. Structure-activity relationship analysis revealed that the electronic and steric characteristics of substituents substantially influenced enzyme inhibitory activity. Molecular docking demonstrated favorable binding orientations. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations provided insights into the electronic properties, frontier molecular orbitals, and chemical reactivity of the active derivatives. Furthermore, in silico ADMET profiling indicated favorable drug-like and pharmacokinetic characteristics. Overall, these findings identify compound 5 and the pyrimidine-oxadiazole scaffold as promising frameworks for further development of dual α-amylase/α-glucosidase inhibitors.

articles.title: Rab32 exacerbates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury via PKA/P300/H3K18la-dependent glucose metabolic reprogramming.
articles.abstract: Glucose metabolic reprogramming, defined by uncoupling between glycolysis and glucose oxidation, is a critical determinant of cardiac dysfunction after ischemia/reperfusion (I/R), yet its upstream drivers remain elusive. RAB32, a mitochondrial Rab GTPase with A-kinase anchoring protein (AKAP) activity, participates in mitochondrial homeostasis, but its role in myocardial I/R injury and glucose metabolic reprogramming is unknown. We used cardiomyocyte-specific RAB32 knockout mice subjected to left anterior descending coronary artery ligation and H9c2 cells exposed to hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R), combined with integrated transcriptomic profiling of I/R myocardium and metabolomic profiling of RAB32-knockdown cardiomyocytes. Using these complementary approaches, we identify RAB32 as a key driver of glucose metabolic reprogramming after I/R. RAB32 was upregulated in I/R myocardium and H/R cardiomyocytes. Cardiomyocyte-specific RAB32 deletion reduced infarct size, decreased CK, cTnI, and LDH levels, preserved cardiac function, and maintained mitochondrial homeostasis. Conversely, RAB32 knockdown attenuated, whereas RAB32 overexpression aggravated, H/R-induced cardiomyocyte injury and mitochondrial dysfunction. Mechanistically, RAB32 bound protein kinase A (PKA) through its AKAP domain, promoting PKA-dependent P300 phosphorylation and H3K18la elevation. H3K18la was enriched at promoter regions of HK2 and PDK4 and drove their transcription; HK2 enhanced glycolysis, whereas PDK4 phosphorylated and inhibited PDHA1, blocking pyruvate oxidation and uncoupling glycolysis from glucose oxidation. RAB32 ablation reversed these metabolic alterations, restoring ATP levels and coupling between glycolysis and glucose oxidation. These findings identify the RAB32/PKA/P300/H3K18la axis as a previously unappreciated epigenetic checkpoint governing glucose metabolic reprogramming in mouse hearts following I/R, nominating RAB32 and its downstream pathway as potential therapeutic targets for myocardial I/R injury.

articles.title: The conversion of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells to eosinophil-like cells exacerbates the progression of pulmonary arterial hypertension with increased secretion of 12-HETE.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterised by progressive pulmonary arterial (PA) vascular remodeling, with abnormal phenotypic transformation of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) playing a central role. Arachidonic acid (AA) metabolites have been implicated in this process, yet the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms by which its metabolite 12-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (12-HETE) contributes to PAH remain incompletely understood. Plasma concentrations of 12-HETE were significantly elevated in PAH patients. In SU5416/hypoxia (SuHx)-induced PAH mouse model, the 12/15-lipoxygenase (12/15-LOX) inhibitor ML-351 markedly attenuated disease progression. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis revealed a unrecognized phenotypic transdifferentiation of a subset of PASMCs into eosinophil-like (Eos-like) cells. Mechanistically, studies utilizing EOS-deficient (ΔdblGATA) mice demonstrated that these newly Eos-like cells, along with native eosinophils (EOS), secrete 12-HETE. In vitro CCK-8 assays confirmed that hypoxia-induced PASMC proliferation was attenuated by the leukotriene B4 receptor 2 (BLT2) antagonist LY255283, confirming that the 12-HETE/BLT2 axis drives PASMC proliferation, thereby creating a positive feedback loop that amplifies vascular remodeling. These findings establish the 12-HETE as a critical mediator of a novel EOS-PASMC signaling axis that drives PA vascular remodeling in PAH. This study highlights a promising new therapeutic strategy for PAH.

articles.title: Houttuynin counteracts osteoporosis by abrogating CHIP-mediated ubiquitination of ESR1 and curtailing osteoclastogenesis.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the protective effects of Houttuynin against postmenopausal osteoporosis and the molecular mechanisms underlying its regulation of osteoclastogenesis. The effects of Houttuynin were assessed in an ovariectomized (OVX) mouse model by evaluating bone mineral density (BMD), trabecular microarchitecture, and hepatic and renal safety. A receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand (RANKL)-induced osteoclast differentiation model was used to examine osteoclast formation and bone resorptive activity. Target identification, protein interaction analysis, ubiquitination assays, and protein stability evaluation were performed to investigate the relationship between Houttuynin and estrogen receptor alpha (ESR1). Houttuynin treatment alleviated OVX-induced bone loss and preserved trabecular microarchitecture. Mechanistically, Houttuynin interacted with ESR1 and reduced carboxyl terminus of Hsp70-interacting protein (CHIP)-mediated ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of ESR1, thereby maintaining its protein stability. Preservation of ESR1 suppressed RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation and bone resorption, whereas ESR1 depletion weakened the inhibitory effects of Houttuynin. No obvious hepatic or renal toxicity was observed following Houttuynin administration. These findings identify ESR1 stabilization as an important mechanism contributing to the anti-osteoporotic effects of Houttuynin. By limiting CHIP-mediated ESR1 degradation, Houttuynin suppresses excessive osteoclast activation and may represent a potential strategy for targeting osteoclast-related bone loss.

articles.title: Blockage of Pcsk6-mediated autophagy is involved in the protection of Znf667 against myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: The objective of this study is to elucidate the function and mechanism of Pcsk6 in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. Serum PCSK6 levels were increased in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction patients following primary percutaneous coronary intervention (p < 0.0001) and positively correlated with cTnI (r = 0.511) and NT-proBNP levels (r = 0.464). Pcsk6 levels were elevated in myocardial tissues 6 h after I/R (p = 0.0001) and cardiomyocytes 12 h after hypoxia-reperfusion (H/R) (p < 0.0001). Pcsk6 knockdown reduced the LC3B-II/I ratio in myocardial tissues and H/R-treated cardiomyocytes (p < 0.0001 and p = 0.0020, respectively) and decreased INF/AAR in mice (p = 0.0303). Conversely, Pcsk6 overexpression increased the LC3B-II/I ratio (p = 0.0338) and reduced cell viability (p = 0.0293) under H/R. Znf667 was downregulated in H/R cardiomyocytes (p = 0.0096). Znf667 overexpression reduced wild-type Pcsk6 promoter activity (p = 0.0004) and Pcsk6 mRNA expression (p = 0.0011). Moreover, Znf667 overexpression reduced INF/AAR in mice (p = 0.0216) and the Nf-κB p-p65/total p65 ratio in H/R cardiomyocytes (p = 0.0164), which were restored by combined overexpression of Pcsk6 (p = 0.0005 and p = 0.0297). In H/R cardiomyocytes overexpressing both Znf667 and Pcsk6, BAY11-7082 increased cell viability (p = 0.0203) and reduced the LC3B-II/I ratio (p = 0.0146). In conclusion, Znf667 alleviates enhanced autophagy and myocardial I/R injury by transcriptionally suppressing Pcsk6. The current findings suggest that Nf-κB may be involved in this process and that PCSK6 may be a biomarker for assessing reperfusion injury.

articles.title: Development of a non-targeted fingerprint profiling LC-HRMS method combined with chemometric analysis as a new approach for the detection of unexpected impurities.
articles.abstract: Valsartan drugs were recalled in 2018 because of the coincidental discovery of unexpected N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA). The fact that NDMA was not detected by the established comprehensive quality control methods is mainly due to the targeted approach applied being devoted to the determination of known and expected impurities. This study examines the use of a non-targeted screening approach to monitor the fingerprint profiles of finished products for unexpected impurities. To this end, we developed a profiling method for ramipril tablets using LC-HRMS coupled with SIMCA (soft independent modelling of class analogies) chemometric analysis. Fingerprint profiles were generated using a pentafluorophenyl reversed phase column with a methanol/water gradient coupled to a qTOF mass spectrometer with electrospray ionization in positive and negative mode. By applying chemometric analysis to the untargeted fingerprint profiles, it was possible to distinguish the fingerprint profiles generated from "clean" and spiked ramipril batches at impurity concentrations as low as 10 µg/L demonstrating the methods suitability for trace-level impurity profiling. SIMCA even allowed the identification of the substances responsible for the deviations in the fingerprint profiles. This study shows that untargeted fingerprint profiling coupled with multivariate data analysis is capable of being applied in addition to existing targeted quality control methods as a proactive approach to detect unexpected impurities instead of reactive batch recalls.

articles.title: Obesity-Induced Alterations in Linezolid Tissue Distribution Revealed by Dynamic Positron Emission Tomography Imaging.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The rising prevalence of obesity and its associated susceptibility to infection raise concerns about the adequacy of fixed linezolid dosing. Obesity-related alterations in tissue drug exposure remain poorly characterised. This study quantified the in vivo biodistribution and pharmacokinetics of linezolid in diet-induced obese and control mice using positron emission tomography (PET). METHODS: Male C57BL/6J mice received a high-fat (n=6) or standard diet (n=8) for ten weeks. [¹⁸F]F-Linezolid was produced by copper-mediated ¹⁸F-fluorination of a boronic ester precursor under optimised low-base conditions. Following intravenous administration, dynamic whole-body PET images were acquired over 90 minutes, followed by computed tomography (CT) imaging. Volumes of interest (brown and subcutaneous white adipose tissue, heart, knee, brain, and lung) were analysed using radioactivity concentration, total radioactivity, standardised uptake values, and kinetic modelling with an image-derived input function. Plasma radiometabolites were quantified by high-performance liquid chromatography. RESULTS: [¹⁸F]F-Linezolid was obtained with >99% radiochemical purity and molar activity of 28-92 GBq/µmol. Obese mice showed lower blood radioactivity, with comparable parent-fraction profiles between groups. The one-tissue compartment model and Logan analysis provided optimal fits. Volume of distribution was significantly reduced in obese animals exclusively in adipose depots, accompanied by lower influx rate constants, whereas exposure was fully preserved in lung, brain, and bone/joint tissue. CONCLUSION: Obesity induces selective pharmacokinetic alterations confined to adipose compartments without compromising linezolid delivery to clinically relevant target tissues, revealing a plasma-tissue dissociation and a tissue-specific distribution that may limit the interpretation of plasma-based therapeutic drug monitoring.

articles.title: Modeling of Eutectic Phase Behavior in Pharmaceutical Mixtures Using the PC-SAFT Equation of State.
articles.abstract: The perturbed-chain statistical associating fluid theory (PC-SAFT) equation of state (EoS) is utilized to estimate eutectic phase behavior in pharmaceutical mixtures. Eutectic formation in pharmaceutical mixtures plays an important role in modifying the melting behavior and solubility of pharmaceuticals. Accurate prediction of eutectic temperature and composition is still challenging due to the presence of strong molecular interactions such as dispersion, chain, repulsion and hydrogen bonding. Drug-drug eutectic systems and drug-deep eutectic solvent (DES) mixtures commonly display V-shaped eutectic phase diagrams. This is due to strong non-ideal interactions in the liquid phase and poor miscibility in the solid state. The SAFT-based models such as the PC-SAFT provides a physically based framework for modeling non-ideal thermodynamic behavior. The molecular interactions between chain-like segments and associating functional groups of drugs and DES molecules were modeled satisfactorily by the PC-SAFT EoS. The pure model parameters have been adjusted using Solid-Liquid Equilibrium (SLE) data at an arbitrary temperature and in various solvents. The obtained parameters have been utilized to predict the eutectic behavior of drug-drug and drug-DES systems. In some cases, a binary interaction coefficient (BIC) was used to improve model performance. PC-SAFT successfully reproduces the eutectic trends observed in pharmaceutical mixtures. The proposed methodology can be used to predict solubility and eutectic phase behavior for drug-drug and drug-DES systems over a wide range of temperatures and molar ratios for newly designed drugs.

articles.title: Folate-chitosan nanoparticles for retinal targeted-delivery of ganciclovir: Preparation, characterization and investigation of their bioactivities.
articles.abstract: Herpes simplex virus (HSV)-1-induced retinitis is a serious ocular infection. Although intravitreal (IVT) injection of ganciclovir (GCV) is currently accepted as one of its treatment methods, frequent IVT injection causes some complications. To overcome this limitation, folate-chitosan nanoparticles containing GCV (GCV-FCS-NPs) were prepared. The objectives of this study were 1) to prepare and characterize GCV-FCS-NPs, 2) to evaluate their in vitro bioactivities, and 3) to assess pharmacokinetics of GCV following IVT injection of GCV-FCS-NPs in the rats' eyes. Folate-chitosan was synthesized via a carbodiimide reaction. Then, GCV-FCS-NPs were prepared by an ionic gelation technique. The obtained GCV-FCS-NPs had a particle size of 195 nm with moderate size distribution and positive charges. Their entrapment efficiency was around 21 %. Cellular uptake studies showed that GCV-FCS-NPs could significantly enhance GCV internalization in the ARPE-19 cells. Their IC50 against HSV-1 was 11.75 ± 1.82 µg/mL. Pharmacokinetic studies demonstrated that GCV-FCS-NPs provided higher AUC and longer half-life of GCV in the vitreous humor when compared to that of GCV from GCV solution. Furthermore, IVT injection of GCV-FCS-NPs did not cause harmful side effects in the rats' eyes. These findings indicate the potential of GCV-FCS-NPs for ocular delivery of GCV via IVT injection.

articles.title: Combining adjustments in both freezing and primary drying for highly efficient lyophilization with insights into porous structure.
articles.abstract: Lyophilization is a long and expensive process. Optimization can reduce both time and cost of particularly the primary drying phase of lyophilization. However, the faster drying risks product collapse, which occurs when the temperature of the formulation exceeds its critical temperature. The objective of the present research was to dramatically enhance the efficiency of the primary drying phase without compromising product temperature. We propose a strategy that integrates the modification of freezing conditions with correspondingly appropriate shelf temperatures during primary drying. The results show that reducing the freezing rate allows for an increase in shelf temperature, thereby increasing the sublimation rate during primary drying, without increasing the product temperature. The pore size of lyophilized cakes frozen at different rates was measured by low-pressure mercury intrusion porosimetry (LP-MIP) and gas adsorption. The median pore diameter by LP-MIP more effectively represented the porous structure as it related to process parameters than did the specific surface area (SSA) obtained from gas adsorption. Altering the freezing to a longer protocol along with raising the shelf temperature during primary drying shortened primary drying by nearly 70% while maintaining the same product temperature by increasing the median pore diameter of the dried cake by 60%. The overall cycle time was reduced by 50%.

articles.title: Porous pH-responsive calcium alginate self-emulsifying gel microspheres as a multistage delivery system: enhanced oral bioavailability of nintedanib via lymphatic absorption.
articles.abstract: This study developed a liquid self-emulsifying drug delivery system (BIBF-SEDDS, size 23.83 nm, zeta 20.5 mV) to enhance nintedanib (BIBF) oral bioavailability. BIBF-SEDDS was encapsulated in pH-sensitive calcium alginate gel microspheres (BIBF-S-SEDDS). Eudragit L100 (precipitation inhibitor) and PEG 400 (porogenic agent) were further added to obtain porous BIBF-S-SEDDS. In vitro dissolution and in vivo pharmacokinetics in rats were compared with imitation soft capsules. Porous BIBF-S-SEDDS increased oral bioavailability by 2.11-fold, prolonged Tmax, reduced gastric irritation (HE staining), and improved intestinal absorption. Liver enzyme (ALT/AST) levels suggested better safety. A chylomicron blockade model indicated lymphatic transport as an auxiliary absorption pathway. Accelerated stability (6 months, 40 °C/75% RH) showed no significant changes in appearance, drug content, or dissolution. This multistage delivery system offers a promising strategy for oral BIBF administration.

articles.title: Effect of uncertainty in probabilistic reinforcement discrimination tasks.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Survival in unpredictable environments requires organisms to distinguish between stochastic noise and fundamental shifts in environmental contingencies. Traditional paradigms like the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT) and reversal learning involve multiple confounding variables, such as simultaneous mixed-valence appraisal and history-dependent procedural shifts, that complicate the isolation of specific cognitive processes. OBJECTIVE: To address these limitations, we developed a stationary probabilistic reinforcement discrimination (PRD) task that isolates appetitive (reward) and aversive (relief-based) reinforcement across separate experiments. Using a trial-by-trial analysis within a Bayesian-inspired framework, we modeled how mice navigate uncertainty by weighting stable, long-term prior beliefs against immediate misleading experiences. RESULTS: Our results demonstrate that environmental uncertainty induced by tempering the salience of outcome feedback, promotes a "stickiness" of previously acquired discrimination, anchoring behaviour to established mental models. This effect was consistent across both appetitive and aversive domains, suggesting that while reward and relief are governed by distinct neurobiological substrates, they are processed through similar mental representations during decision-making. Furthermore, we explored physical effort as a non-verbal proxy for decision confidence, finding that performance variability (amplitude variance), rather than effort magnitude per se, serves as a reliable metric for internal confidence. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that uncertainty effectively shields prior beliefs from the destabilizing effects of recent information, potentially stunting the prediction errors necessary for new learning. By bridging computational modeling with behavioural flexibility, this study establishes the PRD task as a robust platform for investigating the mechanisms of belief updating in both healthy and pathological states.

articles.title: Oxycodone-Related Deaths Identified in Forensic Autopsies in Western Denmark, 2013-2025: A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract: Non-medical use of prescription opioids including oxycodone is an increasing concern in Denmark, particularly among young individuals. The present retrospective observational study aimed to investigate whether the annual number of fatal oxycodone poisonings increased over time in a population of decedents undergoing forensic autopsy in Western Denmark. We used retrospective data from the autopsy reports of all decedents with oxycodone detected in postmortem femoral blood from May 2013 through 2025 (n = 183). Among these, 107 (59%) died from poisoning involving oxycodone. The number of annual oxycodone poisonings increased from four in 2014 to 16 in 2025. The number of decedents with no apparent prescription for oxycodone and decedents with illicit drug use increased as well, and other psychoactive drugs were frequently detected in oxycodone poisonings. Twenty-seven decedents (15%) were young, defined as age ≤ 25 years. Nineteen (70%) of these 27 died from accidental oxycodone poisoning, 16 (84%) during 2020-2025. Attention deficit hyperkinetic disorder was reported as a comorbidity in 10 (37%) of the young decedents. In conclusion, the present study demonstrates an increasing annual number of oxycodone poisonings among forensic autopsy cases in Western Denmark and suggests that further investigations and preventive efforts in the young may be warranted.

articles.title: Proof-of-concept phase II study protocol to evaluate the efficacy and safety of prednisone in the treatment of idiosyncratic hepatotoxicity and its mechanistic pathways through an integrative analysis: the DILICORT clinical trial.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Idiosyncratic drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is an unpredictable adverse reaction ranging from mild liver enzyme elevations to acute liver failure, with management largely limited to withdrawal of the causative drug. An international propensity score-matched study of 724 DILI cases associated corticosteroid therapy with a higher liver enzyme normalization rate, particularly in moderate-to-severe cases without early improvement. These findings informed the design and selection of endpoints for the DILICORT trial, which aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of prednisone in patients with DILI. The trial will also investigate the effects of treatment on liver function recovery and identify biomarkers associated with therapeutic response. METHODS: DILICORT (EUCT 2024-513004-33-00; NCT06251232) is a national, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase II proof-of-concept trial. Sixty patients with moderate-to-severe DILI who show no ≥ 15% reduction in alanine aminotransferase (ALT) or have persistently increasing total bilirubin levels within 5-10 days will be recruited across 15 Spanish centers and followed for 12 weeks. Participants will be randomized to receive a 5-week course of prednisone or matching placebo. The primary objectives are to evaluate prednisone efficacy, assessed by the time to bilirubin reduction or normalization, and its safety and tolerability. Secondary objectives include changes in ALT, aspartate aminotransferase and international normalized ratio, progression to acute liver failure, and health-related quality of life. In addition, there are mechanistic objectives focused on elucidating DILI pathogenesis and biomarker discovery. DISCUSSION: DILICORT is the first multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of prednisone in acute idiosyncratic DILI, designed to provide the highest evidence for this therapeutic approach. It specifically targets patients with moderate-to-severe DILI who do not show a favorable early clinical course and incorporates centralized adjudication of suspected DILI cases. Its integrated mechanistic approach may improve understanding of DILI pathophysiology, identify prognostic and treatment-response biomarkers, and facilitate the development of precision medicine strategies and evidence-based clinical guidelines. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.clinicaltrialsregister.eu/ctr-search/search, identifier EUCT 2024-513004-33-00; https://clinicaltrials.gov/, identifier NCT06251232.

articles.title: Endophytic Berkeleyomyces rouxiae producing podophyllotoxin and deoxypodophyllotoxin with antibacterial, antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Podophyllum hexandrum is a medicinal plant valued for podophyllotoxin and deoxypodophyllotoxin, whose sustainable production remains challenging. Endophytic fungi represent potential alternative sources of these bioactive metabolites. METHODS: Endophytic fungi isolated from P. hexandrum were screened using thin-layer and high-performance liquid chromatography. The promising isolate was characterized using morphological, molecular, chromatographic, and spectroscopic analyses. The antibacterial, antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities of the fungal-derived compounds were evaluated. RESULTS: Among 25 isolates, PH12 was identified as Berkeleyomyces rouxiae, producing podophyllotoxin (53.8 µg/g DW) and deoxypodophyllotoxin (32.3 µg/g DW), with structural analyses confirming metabolite identity. Fungal podophyllotoxin (fPT) and deoxypodophyllotoxin (fDPT) showed IC50 values of 2.491 ± 0.08 and 2.602 ± 0.09 µg/mL against Escherichia coli, and 2.388 ± 0.07 and 2.528 ± 0.07 µg/mL against Staphylococcus aureus, respectively, compared with 2.467 ± 0.08 and 2.519 ± 0.09 µg/mL for their standards against E. coli and 2.243 ± 0.06 and 2.459 ± 0.08 µg/mL against S. aureus. The fPT and fDPT demonstrated concentration-dependent antioxidant activity, with IC50 values of 325.6 and 404.2 µg/mL in the DPPH assay and 339.3 and 465.1 µg/mL in the reducing power assay, compared with 302.7 and 370.9 µg/mL and 306.6 and 439.1 µg/mL for standards. Cytotoxicity against MCF-7 cells showed IC50 values of 1.336 µg/mL for fPT and 18.32 ng/mL for fDPT, comparable to 1.284 µg/mL and 16.46 ng/mL for standards. CONCLUSION: This is among the first reports of B. rouxiae producing both lignans, highlighting its potential as a sustainable source of pharmacologically important compounds with antibacterial, antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities.

articles.title: Multi-omics profiling reveals epigenetic alterations and a candidate SIRT1-β-catenin axis in bakuchiol ferulate-mediated photoaging protection.
articles.abstract: Skin photoaging, driven primarily by ultraviolet A (UVA) exposure, involves extracellular matrix degradation, aberrant inflammation, and multilayered epigenetic dysregulation. Bakuchiol ferulate (BF), a novel ester conjugate of bakuchiol (BAK) and a ferulic acid (FA) analog, was synthesized to combine the beneficial properties of BAK and FA. However, its anti-photoaging efficacy and mechanisms of action remain unexplored. Here, we evaluated BF in a UVA-induced nude mouse model using integrated transcriptomic, DNA methylomic, and miRNA profiling, with BAK, FA, and retinol (ROL) included as comparators. BF dose-dependently attenuated UVA-induced photoaging phenotypes and produced greater improvements than BAK or FA across the endpoints examined. Relative to 0.01% ROL, 0.1% BF showed comparable efficacy, whereas 0.4% BF yielded larger improvements in epidermal thickness, dermal collagen content, and inflammatory markers. These phenotypic effects were accompanied by coordinated epigenetic changes, including alterations in miRNA expression and DNA methylation. Integrative network analysis revealed an association between the SIRT1-β-catenin signaling pathway and BF's anti-photoaging effects. These network-level predictions were in line with molecular observations of β-catenin nuclear accumulation and elevated Cyclin D1 expression, together with reduced miR-34a-5p and miR-450b-3p expression associated with increased SIRT1 and β-catenin protein levels, respectively. Molecular docking further suggested potential binding of BF to SIRT1. Collectively, these findings characterize the multi-layered molecular response to BF in photoaged skin and associate its protective effects with potential engagement of the SIRT1-β-catenin axis. These findings underscore molecular grafting as a rational strategy for engineering phytochemical derivatives with enhanced anti-photoaging profiles, expanding the chemical space of natural product-based skin protective agents.

articles.title: Pharmacogenomic predictors of proton pump inhibitor response in pediatric eosinophilic esophagitis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Genetic variability has been implicated in the heterogeneous response to proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) in eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE), with variants in CYP2C19 and STAT6 previously associated with treatment outcome. However, the broader pharmacogenomic determinants underlying interindividual variability in PPI response remain incompletely understood. METHODS: This study aimed to investigate whether genetic variability in Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion (ADME) genes contributes to PPI response in pediatric EoE. Fifty-eight patients (17 responders, PPI-RE, and 41 non-responders, PPI-NORE) were genotyped using the Drug Metabolizing Enzymes and Transporters (DMET) Plus microarray, covering 231 ADME-related genes. Genetic and clinical data were integrated using a machine learning-based approach to explore determinants of treatment response. RESULTS: CHST3 rs4148944 G/G genotype showed the strongest nominal association with PPI response (p < 0.0064). Integrative analysis revealed combinatorial patterns involving CHST3, CHST11 gene (rs7847), SULT1A2/A3 (rs11859842), and NR1I3 (rs55802895), particularly in the presence of food allergy, which improved patient stratification. Although these additional variants were not individually significant, their combined occurrence-especially in association with food allergy-suggests a potential contribution of both metabolic and regulatory pathways to PPI response variability. CONCLUSION: Overall, this study provides exploratory, proof-of-concept evidence that the CHST3 rs4148944 G/G genotype, together with other genetic variants and clinical features, may influence PPI response in EoE and contribute to patient stratification. These findings support the potential of integrative pharmacogenomic approaches, although validation in larger cohorts is required.

articles.title: Comparison of subcutaneous and intravenous administration of the monoclonal antibody CSX-1004 on fentanyl-induced respiratory depression in squirrel monkeys.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fentanyl and related synthetic opioids remain major contributors to overdose mortality, primarily through opioid-induced respiratory depression. CSX-1004 is a fully human monoclonal antibody designed to bind fentanyl in the peripheral circulation and prevent its entry into the brain. This study evaluated the pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) equivalence of intravenous (IV) and subcutaneous (SC) administration of CSX-1004 in squirrel monkeys and established a population PK (PopPK) model to support route extrapolation. METHODS: Protection against fentanyl-induced respiratory depression was assessed after administration of 40 mg/kg CSX-1004 using whole-body plethysmography over 28 days. Serum antibody concentrations were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and PK parameters were characterized using noncompartmental and PopPK analyses. RESULTS: Both IV and SC administration produced substantial and durable attenuation of fentanyl-induced respiratory depression, resulting in a greater than 10-fold rightward shift in fentanyl potency that persisted for up to 28 days. SC CSX-1004 administration exhibited a maximum concentration of 491.7 ± 50.4 μg/mL at 48.0 ± 19.6 h (Tmax) and an absolute bioavailability of 92.0% based on   A U C 0 - ∞    . Terminal half-life was comparable between routes (∼272 h). A two-compartment PopPK model with first-order absorption and elimination adequately described the concentration-time data and demonstrated robust predictive performance. Serum concentrations and respiratory protection were lower after SC than after IV administration during the first 24-48 h, reflecting the absorption phase, and converged from Day 2 onward. Simulations indicated that SC and IV administration achieved overlapping systemic exposures beyond the absorption phase and equivalent concentrations associated with sustained respiratory protection through Day 28. CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that SC administration of CSX-1004 provides PK and PD outcomes comparable to IV dosing, once absorption is complete, supporting SC delivery as a practical and clinically feasible approach for long-acting prophylaxis against fentanyl-induced respiratory depression.

articles.title: Resveratrol alleviates glucolipid metabolism disorders in diabetic nephropathy via the HIF-1α pathway: a network pharmacology and experimental validation study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) represents a major microvascular complication of diabetes with complex pathogenesis. Resveratrol (RSV), a polyphenol from Polygonum cuspidatum, is a potential therapeutic agent for DN. However, the exact mechanisms of RSV modulating glucolipid metabolism in DN remain unclear. METHODS: Potential targets and signaling pathways of RSV against DN were predicted by network pharmacology and molecular docking. Based on the prediction, a DN model was generated in male Wistar rats using a high-fat diet/streptozotocin (HFD/STZ) induction, followed by 12-week RSV (30 mg/kg/d) for in vivo validation. In vitro, HK-2 cells cultured in palmitic acid (PA) were treated with either RSV or LW6, a hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) inhibitor. Biochemical parameters, histopathological alterations and lipid deposition were examined. AKT/HIF-1α pathway activation and downstream metabolic gene levels were analyzed via Western blot, immunofluorescence and RT-qPCR. RESULTS: Bioinformatics findings revealed RSV exerts its anti-DN effects predominantly through the prioritized candidate AKT1 and the highly enriched HIF-1 signaling pathway. In vivo, RSV significantly ameliorated hyperglycemia and renal dysfunction and alleviated histopathological injuries and glycogen storage. Mechanistically, RSV suppressed p-AKT and HIF-1α expression, reduced Glut1 mRNA levels, and elevated Ldlr mRNA levels, significantly. In vitro, RSV effectively decreased lipid accumulation and inhibited HIF-1α expression, downregulating SREBP1, SREBP2, LDLR, GLUT1 and TGF-β1 and upregulating INSIG2. The effects of LW6 were largely consistent with those of RSV but failed to reduce HIF-1α mRNA levels. CONCLUSION: The attenuation of glucolipid metabolic disorders in DN by RSV is associated with suppression of the HIF-1α pathway, highlighting the therapeutic potential of RSV for DN.

articles.title: Network toxicology, molecular docking and in vitro validation reveal the molecular mechanisms of bisphenol A-induced MASLD.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine-disrupting chemical, is associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. METHODS: This study combined network toxicology and molecular docking to explore BPA-induced hepatotoxicity targets and pathways in MASLD. BPA and MASLD-related targets were screened from multiple databases, with 886 and 3109 targets identified respectively; their intersection targets were analyzed via protein-protein interaction (PPI) network, and core targets were screened using Cytoscape Molecular Complex Detection (MCODE). The GSE163211 dataset was used for external validation of core genes, followed by Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses, and molecular docking verified the binding affinity between BPA and key core targets. RESULTS: We obtained 451 intersection targets, with 16 core targets (e.g., JUN, IL6, TNF, TLR4) identified; Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) validation confirmed significantly upregulated expression of several core targets in MASLD samples (P < 0.05). GO enrichment revealed involvement in transcriptional regulation, protein binding and intracellular structural processes, while KEGG enrichment highlighted the PI3K-Akt, FoxO and cellular senescence pathways. Molecular docking showed BPA bound strongly to six key core targets with binding energies ranging from -5.3 to -8.2 kcal/mol. CONCLUSION: This study identifies the core targets and signaling pathways mediating BPA-induced MASLD, establishing an integrated computational framework for risk assessment of environmental hepatotoxicants and providing a theoretical basis for BPA regulatory policy formulation and MASLD mechanistic research.

articles.title: Wei-Mi-Shu Decoction ameliorates gastric mucosal injury in chronic gastritis with liver-stomach disharmony syndrome through the gut microbiota-hepatic bile acid metabolism axis.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic gastritis (CG) is a high-incidence disease in the digestive system, and liverstomach disharmony syndrome (LSD) is a relatively common syndrome type. This study aimed to evaluate the role and possible mechanism of traditional Chinese medicine Wei-Mi-Shu Decoction (WMS) in treating LSDCG. METHODS: The CG and LSDCG animal models were established and treated with WMS to observe the TCM syndrome scores and behavioral changes, histopathological alterations of the gastric mucosa, and expressions of pro-inflammatory cytokines and tight junction proteins. Then, the changes of gut microbiota and bile acids (BAs) were analyzed by microbiota sequencing and mass spectrometry, and the protein expressions of BA receptors were detected by immunohistochemistry and WB. Finally, Lgr5-positive (Lgr5+) gastric cells were observed by immunofluorescence staining, the expression of gastric mucosal cell differentiation markers was detected by RT-qPCR, and the fatty acid oxidation (FAO) of Lgr5+ cells was observed by fluorescence double staining. RESULTS: WMS reduced the TCM syndrome scores, increased the autonomous activity ability, and improved gastric mucosal injury, inflammatory response, and gastric mucosal barrier disruption in the CG and LSDCG model rats. WMS also regulated the intestinal microbiota and BA metabolism of model rats, and promoted the levels of PPARα and RXR. In addition, WMS attenuated the loss of Lgr5+ gastric stem cells and promoted their differentiation and FAO. CONCLUSION: In conclusion, WMS promoted the differentiation of Lgr5+ gastric stem cells, potentially involving the gut microbiotahepatic BA metabolism axis to repair gastric mucosal injury in LSDCG.

articles.title: Spartina anglica extract attenuates TNF-α/IFN-γ-induced inflammatory responses in HaCaT keratinocytes through suppression of the MAPK, NF-κB, and STAT1 signaling pathways.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the anti-inflammatory effects of Spartina anglica extract (SAE) in a human keratinocyte model of inflammation. HaCaT cells were stimulated with tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and interferon-γ (IFN-γ) to induce inflammatory responses. Cell viability was assessed using the MTT assay to determine non-cytotoxic concentrations. The expression of the chemokines TARC/CCL17 and macrophage-derived chemokine MDC/CCL22 was quantified at both the mRNA and protein levels using quantitative real-time PCR and ELISA, respectively. In addition, the activation of key inflammatory signaling pathways was evaluated by Western blot analysis. SAE did not exhibit cytotoxic effects at concentrations up to 250 μg/mL. Under inflammatory conditions, SAE significantly reduced the expression of CCL17 and CCL22 in a dose-dependent manner. Mechanistically, this suppression was associated with decreased phosphorylation of MAPK signaling components, including ERK, JNK, and p38, as well as inhibition of NF-κB and STAT1 activation. High-performance liquid chromatography analysis revealed a major peak corresponding to the retention time of iso-orientin in SAE. These findings suggest that SAE may attenuate keratinocyte-mediated inflammatory responses through modulation of chemokine expression and key intracellular signaling pathways.

articles.title: Machine-learning-assisted target prioritization and experimental validation of the neoeriocitrin-mTOR axis in impaired osteogenic differentiation.
articles.abstract: Neoeriocitrin (NEO) is a citrus-derived flavonoid with potential osteoprotective activity, but its pharmacological targets and mechanisms in impaired osteogenic differentiation remain unclear. Osteoporosis-related differentially expressed genes were intersected with predicted NEO targets, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, random forest, and support vector machine analyses consistently prioritized MTOR for mechanistic investigation. Molecular docking predicted a favorable binding pose of NEO at the 12-kDa FK506-binding protein (FKBP12)-mTOR FKBP12-rapamycin-binding (FRB) interface, while the cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) demonstrated increased cellular thermal stability of mTOR following NEO treatment, supporting an mTOR-associated intracellular effect. In dexamethasone-treated bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, NEO dose-dependently restored alkaline phosphatase activity, mineralized nodule formation, and the expression of runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2), osteopontin (OPN), and alkaline phosphatase (ALP). NEO also enhanced autophagic flux, increased the microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 beta (LC3B)-II/LC3B-I ratio, reduced p62 expression, and suppressed dexamethasone-induced phosphorylation of mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) and ribosomal protein S6 kinase 1 (S6K1). Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy with 3-methyladenine (3-MA) and mTOR overexpression both attenuated the pro-osteogenic effects of NEO. Collectively, these findings support an mTORC1-associated S6K1 signaling mechanism linking NEO treatment to autophagy regulation and osteogenic differentiation. NEO may therefore represent a candidate natural compound for further preclinical investigation in osteoporosis-related bone loss.

articles.title: An immune-resistance dual-axis framework prioritizes MAL2 for functional investigation in lung cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint blockade has reshaped lung cancer treatment, yet durable benefit remains restricted to a subset of patients. Biomarkers incompletely capture interactions between immune activation and tumor-intrinsic resistance. Integrating immune and epithelial expression programs may help identify response-associated states and candidates for functional investigation. METHODS: Public bulk transcriptomes were analyzed with format-specific preprocessing, empirical Bayes differential expression, standardized cross-cohort evidence, and gene-set enrichment. Five discovery-informed modules formed an immune-resistance score. Conditional leave-one-out and leave-cohort-out analyses refitted normalization within training data and compared the fixed score with a nested ridge-logistic model. Survival, composition-adjustment, and prioritization sensitivity analyses were performed. Single-cell counts underwent quality control, unsupervised clustering, and patient-level pseudobulk analysis. MAL2 was investigated in A549 and H1299 cells using knockdown, growth, motility, apoptosis, HLA-ABC, cytokine, and PBMC co-culture assays. RESULTS: No individual gene met FDR <0.05 in any of the three discovery contrasts. Favorable-response genes were enriched for adaptive immune processes, whereas the unfavorable list showed weaker DNA-replication enrichment. Conditional leave-cohort-out AUCs for the dual-axis score were 0.964, 0.859, and 0.773; performance did not consistently exceed the immune axis. In GSE190266, outcome analysis yielded a cohort-relative AUC of 0.617 with incomplete module coverage. Higher scores were associated with longer PFS in two evaluated cohorts. Quality control retained 91,762 single cells. MAL2 remained epithelial-enriched and ranked third among 58 evaluable candidates, but its patient-level epithelial response contrast and standalone PFS associations were not significant. Knockdown reduced growth and motility-related readouts, increased apoptosis and HLA-ABC expression, and altered cytokine and co-culture activation readouts. CONCLUSION: The immune-resistance framework links cohort-level response patterns to epithelial candidates for functional investigation. MAL2 depletion alters growth and immune-related phenotypes in lung cancer cells, supporting further investigation of its biological role.

articles.title: Safety evaluation of genipin in Beagle dogs: acute and 28-day repeated oral toxicity studies.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Genipin, a typical iridoid constituent derived from the fruits of Gardenia jasminoides Ellis, is an essential in vivo metabolite of geniposide. It exhibits diverse potent biofunctions, including hepatoprotection, anti-inflammation, neuroprotection, antioxidation, and glycolipid metabolism modulation. Nevertheless, the systemic toxicological profile of genipin remains insufficiently characterized, with particularly limited safety evidence from non-rodent models. This study aimed to evaluate the acute and subacute oral toxicity of genipin in Beagle dogs as a preclinical safety assessment. METHODS: Acute toxicity was assessed using single oral doses of genipin at 29, 41, 59, 84, 120, and 140 mg/kg. For subacute toxicity, repeated-dose groups were administered 3, 9, and 27 mg/kg/day for 28 days. Clinical signs, body weight, food intake, hematology, clinical chemistry, urinalysis, electrocardiography, fecal occult blood, and histopathology were evaluated. RESULTS: The results showed that the oral approximate lethal dose of genipin was 120.0-140.0 mg/kg, with doses ≥41 mg/kg inducing thymic, hepatorenal, and gallbladder toxicity. Repeated 27 mg/kg/day genipin caused gastrointestinal irritation, anemia, prolonged coagulation parameters, and toxicity to the hepatobiliary system, thymus, bone marrow, and gonads; 3 and 9 mg/kg/day genipin induced mild male gonad toxicity. Bone marrow toxicity and gastric mucosal irritation were fully reversible after recovery, while hepatic, thymic, and gonadal toxicity showed partial recovery. CONCLUSION: This study clarified the dose-toxicity relationship, major target organs, and toxic reversibility of genipin following oral exposure in non-rodent species. These findings provide robust preclinical toxicological evidence to support rational dosage optimization, risk assessment, and the safe use of genipin.

articles.title: An Integrated Network of Classical Endocrine and Retinoic Acid Pathways Reveals Points of Convergence and Knowledge Gaps.
articles.abstract: Adverse outcome pathways (AOPs) are pragmatic descriptions of how molecular perturbations can lead to adverse effects in intact organisms. To examine connectivity across endocrine signalling pathways, we integrated 117 AOPs related to oestrogen, androgen, steroidogenesis, thyroid and retinoic acid (EATS,R) modalities into a unified endocrine AOP network (AOPN). The resulting network revealed uneven pathway representation, limited mechanistic integration across EATS,R modalities and substantial gaps in certain signalling coverage, with only six retinoic acid-related AOPs available for integration. At the same time, the AOPN identified highly connected biological nodes linking multiple pathways to adverse outcomes, highlighting potential points of endocrine crosstalk as well as cross-species key events (KEs), bridging human and environmental health. To strengthen retinoid pathway integration, new KEs describing altered retinoic acid receptor activation were developed as potential network hubs (KE 2419 and KE 2420). Collectively, these findings demonstrate how the AOPN reveals emergent biological relationships, exposes knowledge gaps and identifies candidate targets for NAM development, providing a framework that could be used to prioritise future AOP development, and overall, to support a more integrated, system-level approach to endocrine disruptor identification.

articles.title: Machine learning-driven prediction of protein kinase-ligand binding affinity using extended connectivity interaction features.
articles.abstract: Protein kinases are key cellular regulators of growth, proliferation, and signal transduction, making them important therapeutic targets in precision medicine, particularly for cancer and inflammatory diseases. Although molecular docking remains a central tool in structure-based drug discovery, its predictive accuracy is often limited by rigid receptor assumptions and simplified solvent representation. To overcome these limitations, machine learning models were developed based on Extended Connectivity Interaction Features to predict kinase-ligand binding affinities. A kinase-specific dataset of 2337 complexes from PDBbind 2020 was used to train five regression models, namely Decision Tree, Support Vector Regressor, Gradient Boosting Regressor, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting, using a merged descriptor set of 1757 interaction-specific and physicochemical features. Integration of RDKit descriptors consistently improved predictive performance across models. Among the evaluated models, GBR achieved the highest predictive correlation, with a PCC of 0.72 and R2 value of 0.51, while SVR yielded the lowest mean squared error value of 0.84 with a PCC of 0.71. The XGBoost and RF followed with R2 values of 0.49 and 0.42, respectively, whereas DT showed the weakest performance, with an R2 value of 0.25 and a PCC of 0.54. External validation on 5265 complexes further confirmed the robustness of the framework and facilitated the identification of high-confidence binding candidates through consensus prediction. Notably, this strategy accurately predicted binding affinities and enabled prioritization of the top 20 compounds as potential kinase-binding leads, demonstrating a scalable and computationally efficient framework for improved virtual screening and hit prioritization in rational drug discovery.

articles.title: Sertraline disassembles the mitochondrial transduceosome and disrupts testosterone biosynthesis.
articles.abstract: The widespread use of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) sertraline is limited by its frequent side effect of sexual dysfunction, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study aimed to elucidate how sertraline directly disrupts testicular testosterone synthesis. Using an integrated approach combining network toxicology, molecular docking, in-vivo mouse model, and in-vitro Leydig cells experiments, we identified that clinical doses of sertraline significantly suppressed testosterone synthesis. Mechanistically, sertraline downregulated the protein level of the steroidogenic acute regulatory (StAR), the rate-limiting enzyme for testosterone synthesis, without affecting its mRNA level. Molecular docking and thermal shift assays revealed that sertraline specifically binds to the outer mitochondrial membrane protein VDAC1 with high affinity. This binding site spatially overlapped with the StAR-VDAC1 interaction interface. Consequently, sertraline disrupted the formation of the StAR-VDAC1 transduceosome, as validated by co-immunoprecipitation analysis. This led to StAR destabilization and degradation, thereby blocking mitochondrial cholesterol import and subsequently testosterone biosynthesis. Crucially, VDAC1 overexpression rescued sertraline-induced downregulation of StAR and restored testosterone synthesis. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that sertraline disrupts testosterone synthesis by binding to VDAC1, disrupting the essential StAR-VDAC1 interaction and leading to StAR degradation. This mechanism provides a new perspective for understanding the clinical reproductive-related side effects of sertraline and for developing intervention strategies targeting the VDAC1-StAR interaction.

articles.title: Celastrus orbiculatus Thunb. stem extract attenuates cigarette smoke-induced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in mice by modulating PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Celastrus orbiculatus Thunb. (COT) is a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), with its root, stem, and leaf being used for medicinal purposes. COT characterized by the efficacy of dispelling wind-dampness, invigorating blood, and relieving pain, traditional records in Quanzhou Bencao document the use for asthma, indicating that its traditional treatment in lung system disorders. Previous pharmacological studies have demonstrated that the COT stem (COTS) exhibits anti-inflammatory and protective effects in experimental models related to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, the systemically efficacy and molecular mechanisms underlying the anti-COPD effects of COTS remain poorly understood.
